evidence: Receiving DO online sensor at t=48.0 h drops to 3.06 mg/L (vs ~11.7 mg/L at t=47.8 h), then hovers 1.70–2.94 mg/L through t=51.8 h
Multiple post-48 h DO readings below the 2 mg/L hard limit: 2.12 (48.8 h), 2.00 (50.2 h), 1.96 (51.6 h), 1.70 (51.8 h) under KEEP
Source batches (source-1/2/3) show no such late DO crash at equivalent times (~9–10 mg/L), indicating receiving-process-specific oxygen stress
Delayed product assay on receiving: P rising normally (0 → 0.995 → 2.72 g/L at t=47.8 h), so feed-driven production is healthy and should be retained
allowed_actions: increase_air = [1.0, 1.15] raises air transfer 15% with feed unchanged, expected DO ~2.3–3.3 mg/L on observed baseline
args.rationale: Receiving DO crashed at 48.0 h to ~2-3 mg/L and now oscillates at/below the 2 mg/L hard limit under KEEP (readings of 2.12, 1.96, 1.70 mg/L at 48.8, 51.6, 51.8 h). A plan that keeps DO >= 2 mg/L at every remaining time is required. increase_air raises oxygen transfer by 15% with no feed reduction, predicted to lift DO to ~2.3-3.3 mg/L on the current baseline, satisfying the constraint while retaining full feed and hence product mass. reduce_feed or combined would also add margin but sacrifice product mass unnecessarily; stop yields zero production despite a recoverable oxygen deficit. Source batches show no analogous crash, so this is receiving-process-specific oxygen-transfer insufficiency, best addressed by aeration.
args.uncertainty: The 15% air-increase margin is estimated from observed DO baseline; model mismatch or unobserved state (e.g., higher actual OUR) could keep DO near 2. If subsequent DO readings under the intervention remain marginal, a combined (0.8 feed, 1.15 air) plan would be the fallback. No physics model tool was available; forecast is trend-based and subject to error. No physical safety guarantee is established.
